subject.title: Add an FxTwitter read transport for public lookups, threads, profiles, and search

question: Should Birdclaw core support an explicitly selected FxTwitter/FxEmbed public read transport and own its third-party privacy, endpoint-trust, reliability, configuration, and compatibility obligations?
rationale: The architecture can host the adapter, but source inspection cannot decide whether a public third-party service is an endorsed core transport or whether the long-term operational and privacy contract is acceptable.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core MVP
options.body: Approve an opt-in public-read adapter limited to the documented MVP operations, with no implicit fallback and strict capability, privacy, URL-safety, and fixture-test requirements.

options.title: Keep authenticated transports only
options.body: Decline the integration so core continues to support live X data only through the existing authenticated transport model.

options.title: Request an extension boundary first
options.body: Defer the provider itself and first define a supported external transport/plugin interface that can host FxTwitter without adding the service to core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core MVP
recommendation.body: Approve an opt-in public-read adapter limited to the documented MVP operations, with no implicit fallback and strict capability, privacy, URL-safety, and fixture-test requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes Birdclaw's supported transport and privacy contract, and steipete owns the repository, product vision, and release direction.
